basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 19.' and it opens '(Vers. 19.) Gad latrunculus latrocinabitur eum, et ipse latrocinabitur plantam. Juxta'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 19.) Gad latrunculus latrocinabitur eum, et ipse latrocinabitur plantam. Juxta Hebraeum interpretati sumus. Sed ubi nos latrunculum posuimus, ibi scriptum est GEDUD (גדוד), ut ad GAD nomen alluderet, qui significantius εὔζωνος, id est, accinctus, sive expeditus exprimi potest. Totum autem illud est, quod Ruben, et dimidiam tribum Manasse, ad filios, quos trans Jordanem in possessionem dimiserat, post quatuordecim annos revertens, praelium adversum eos gentium vicinarum grande repererit, et victis hostibus, fortiter dimicarit. Lege librum Jesu Nave (Josue XIII), et Paralipomenon I, V). Non ignoro plura in benedictionibus patriarcharum esse mysteria, sed ad praesens opusculum non pertinet.
